title: Introduce token-affinity meters and compact cost signatures for long-tail observability
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Context: Production customers report noisy long-tail attribution for token-level cost and latency, especially when prompts cross KV-cache boundaries and when short auxiliary tokens dominate cost noise.
Motivation: provide a compact, indexable signal that (1) ties latency/cost to token affinity groups (e.g., system prompts, user prefix, user continuation, tool calls) and (2) produces a lightweight per-request signature that can be stored in traces and aggregated efficiently for dashboards and alerts.
This PR introduces two pieces: token-affinity meters (runtime instrumentation that tags token spans with an affinity label and local cost weight) and compact cost signatures (a fixed-size, base64-encoded summary included as a trace/log annotation).
Summary of changes:
- runtime: observability/metrics/token_affinity_meter.go: new meter to classify tokens into affinity buckets and emit per-span counters and reservoir samples.
- collector: observability/collector/compact_cost_signature.go: implements incremental signature builder (sketch + small histogram) and base64 encoder used in traces/logs.
- console: console/dashboards/token_affinity_dashboard.json: new dashboard with per-affinity P50/P95/P99 latency and cost share, plus a compact signature explorer.
- tracing: tracing/span_enrichers/affinity_enricher.go: attaches compact signature and affinity tags to sampling spans.
- alerts: observability/alerts/affinity_slo_rules.yaml: tuned alert thresholds to suppress high-cardinality noise via signature-based aggregation and reservoir sampling.
- docs: docs/observability/token-affinity.md: motivation, interpretation, and query examples.
- tests: tests/integration/test_token_affinity.py and tests/e2e/affinity_smoke.sh.
Checklist:
- [x] implementation and unit tests
- [x] integration tests (local)
- [x] perf microbench (see performance notes)
- [x] docs and dashboard JSON
- [x] feature-flag gated rollout plan
Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag REDWOOD_OBS_TOKEN_AFFINITY (default off). Staged rollout: enable in staging -> 10% of canary -> 50% -> 100% after 72h. Backout: disable flag and clear local reservoirs; signature format has version header for safe backcompat.
Testing & validation:
- unit tests for meter classification and signature encoding.
- integration test replays sample prompts (see tests/integration) and validates signature invariants (idempotence given identical tokenization and affinity rules).
- canary perf microbench: median CPU overhead ~0.6% at P99 request rate; memory delta ~3% per serving worker; p50 latency increase <1ms.
Observability consequences: compact signatures are small (32–48 bytes) and added to span tags and logs; ingestion cost increase estimated ~0.5% for traces. The collector compacts signatures again at ingestion to remove duplicates.
How to use (examples):
- Console: open "Token Affinity" dashboard and use the signature explorer to search recent 24h sessions by signature.
- Traces: filter by span.tag[affinity.signature]=="<base64>" to find sessions that share cost profile.
Related: ENG-4921 (long-tail attribution), ENG-4988 (kv-cache cross-boundary noise).
Links: internal doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4921; dashboard sample: console/dashboards/token_affinity_dashboard.json
Notes: this PR intentionally keeps affinity buckets coarse (system|prefix|continuation|tool|output) to limit cardinality. Future work: automatic bucket calibration, probabilistic prefix grouping, and integrating signature-based deduping into billing pipelines.

Jun-Woo Lee: Concerned about cardinality if we allow user-defined buckets. Request to add reservoir sampling to the meter. Aisha: implemented reservoir sampler and added integration test; see commit f2c1c8b.
release_notes: Added token-affinity meters and compact cost signatures for improved long-tail cost/latency attribution. Feature-gated rollout; no billing changes. Dashboard and docs included.
notes: This change is observable-safe: signature attaches a short version header and is only used for aggregation/indexing. We will monitor trace ingestion and SLO noise for two weeks post-rollout.
manual_steps: To enable in staging: set REDWOOD_OBS_TOKEN_AFFINITY=true in deployment config and apply observability/alerts/affinity_slo_rules.yaml. Run tests/integration/test_token_affinity.py against staging endpoint.
